items.title: AI tool detects unusual satellite behavior to improve space safety
items.summary: A new AI model can monitor satellites and spot anomalies in their behavior, reducing the risk of in-orbit collisions, according to new research published in the journal Expert Systems.

items.title: Ten-channel photonic interface links neutral-atom qubits in parallel
items.summary: A research group in Japan has demonstrated a world-record 10-channel multiplexed quantum photonic interface based on an integrated waveguide array, a key technology for optically interconnecting multiple quantum computers. The study is published in the journal Optica.

items.title: 9/11 responders passed effects of trauma to their children, study finds
items.summary: Although it's been 25 years since the World Trade Center collapsed after terrorists flew commercial airplanes into each of the center's two towers, the trauma experienced by many first responders and recovery workers is still being felt by their children.

items.title: Non-police safety practitioners reduce crime
items.summary: Non-police community guardians can effectively reduce crime by building relationships in urban disorder hotspots, according to a study.

items.title: Geomagnetic superstorm shook GPS accuracy across the US—its timing may have averted agricultural losses
items.summary: On Nov. 11, 2025, Earth experienced a severe geomagnetic storm triggered by solar flares and coronal mass ejections from an active sunspot region. items.title: Largest review finds formal ethics education improves students' moral reasoning
items.summary: How important is it that kids learn to tell right from wrong? Businessman and former university chancellor David Gonski recently called for ethics classes to be rolled out in all Australian schools to boost social cohesion.

items.title: Anti-influenza therapies that target the host
items.summary: A drug that targets the host rather than the virus could get around the problem of antiviral resistance. Every year, hundreds of thousands of people die of seasonal influenza caused by infection with influenza A and B viruses.

items.title: UK chalks up hottest summer on record for second year running
items.summary: Britain experienced its hottest summer on record for the second year in a row, the UK's national weather agency announced Tuesday, after weeks of successive heat waves and widespread drought conditions.

items.title: Experiment sees surprising result in search for dark matter
items.summary: For the better part of a century, people have been trying to understand dark matter. This invisible substance makes up roughly 85% of the mass in the universe but has never been directly detected. Determining exactly what it is remains one of the biggest questions about our world.

items.title: For a century, journalists have had a voluntary ethics code. Editors are giving it an AI-era reboot
items.summary: Walk into a corner of a newsroom somewhere and you can often find it affixed to a bulletin board, perhaps peeking out from behind the coffee pot: the Society of Professional Journalists's Code of Ethics. It's less than a thousand words, fitting neatly on a poster.
